summary.text: Quartz is a hard mineral made of silica, its atoms joined in a continuous framework of silicon–oxygen tetrahedra that gives the formula SiO₂.
It is the second most common mineral in Earth's lithosphere, making up about 12% of its mass, and it defines the value 7 on the Mohs hardness scale.
At 573 °C it abruptly switches from α-quartz to β-quartz, and the volume change that comes with it can crack ceramics and rocks.

items.prompt: The Greek word that gave us 'crystal' was applied to quartz because some ancient thinkers believed quartz was really what?

options.label: Molten glass that had slowly cooled
Ice frozen so hard it never melts
Tree resin hardened over centuries
Salt left behind by dried seawater

items.explain: Some Greek philosophers thought quartz was supercooled ice, and Pliny the Elder also believed it was permanently frozen ice.

items.prompt: A potter fires clay that contains quartz grains, and tiny cracks appear as the kiln passes about 573 °C. What most likely caused them?

options.label: The quartz grains melted and ran into the clay
The quartz released trapped water as steam
The quartz changed form and its volume shifted
The quartz reacted with oxygen and burned away

items.explain: At 573 °C α-quartz turns into β-quartz, and the significant volume change that comes with it can cause microfracturing in ceramics during firing.

items.prompt: On the Mohs scratch test, an unknown mineral leaves a scratch on quartz. What does that tell you about its Mohs value?

options.label: It is exactly 7, the same as quartz
It is below 7, softer than quartz
Nothing, since scratches do not measure hardness
It is above 7, harder than quartz

items.explain: The Mohs scale ranks hardness by scratching, and quartz defines the value 7, so anything able to scratch it sits higher.

items.prompt: You compare a thumb-sized quartz crystal with one as long as your arm. How do the angles where their long prism faces meet compare?

options.label: They are identical in both crystals
The bigger crystal has wider angles
The smaller crystal has wider angles
They vary randomly between crystals

items.explain: Nicolas Steno found that whatever a quartz crystal's size or shape, its long prism faces always meet at 60°.

items.prompt: Amethyst is purple while rock crystal is colorless, yet both are quartz. What makes the difference?

options.label: Amethyst grows in a different crystal system
Impurities make it absorb some visible light
Its larger crystals bend light more strongly
It formed as β-quartz at high temperature

items.explain: Pure quartz is colorless; impurities change how it absorbs visible light, and the wavelengths left unabsorbed give the color.

items.prompt: You press hard on a quartz crystal fitted with metal contacts on two sides. What do the contacts pick up?

options.label: A brief flash of visible light
A burst of heat from friction
An electric voltage across the crystal
A weak magnetic field around it

items.explain: Quartz is piezoelectric: mechanical stress makes it develop an electric potential.
